sections.h2: How do you sell a house fast in the city of Homestead, FL?
sections.html:
You pick a buyer type, gather the title and lien paperwork, and sign a deed that is witnessed, taxed and recorded in Miami-Dade County. The speed comes from the buyer you choose and how clean the title is, not from any shortcut around the recording steps.

Three routes are common in South Dade. A listed sale reaches the most buyers but depends on a lender's appraisal and inspection timing. A cash purchase removes the lender and often the repair negotiation. A sale to a family member is allowed too, but a transfer for money still carries deed tax, and Florida's Department of Revenue notes there is no special exemption for estate planning transfers.

  • Check who is on title and whether any owner is deceased or out of state.
  • Request payoff letters for every mortgage, home equity line or lien.
  • Ask the tax collector for the current bill and any unpaid years.

sections.h2: What is the city of Homestead like for a home seller?
sections.html:
Homestead is the second oldest city in Miami-Dade County, according to its own history page. South Dade opened to homesteaders in 1898, Henry Flagler's railroad extension brought workers who stayed, and the Town of Homestead was incorporated in 1913 with 121 people. It became a city in 1923.

Hurricane Andrew struck the city directly in 1992, and the Homestead-Miami Speedway broke ground the next year and held its first race in 1995. The city's timeline also lists a voter-approved downtown revitalization, a new City Hall that opened in 2016, and the Seminole Theatre reopening in 2015.

Census numbers for the city show rapid change. The population was 60,512 in 2010 and 80,737 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate is 86,242, a 6.8 percent rise from the 2020 base. Households average 3.21 people, and the owner-occupied rate for 2020 to 2024 is 48.3 percent, so renters are a slight majority. The median owner-occupied home value is $380,000 and median gross rent is $1,674.

sections.h2: How does Homestead's mix of owners and renters affect a sale?
sections.html:
With fewer than half of homes owner-occupied, many Homestead sellers are landlords or heirs who have never lived in the house. That shapes which tax rules matter and what a buyer will ask about.

Landlords should know that Miami-Dade's property appraiser warns owners not to jeopardize a homestead exemption by renting the property. If an exemption was claimed while the house was rented, the appraiser's page says back taxes can run for 10 years, with 15 percent interest per year and a 50 percent penalty. Talk to a Florida attorney before you sell if that could apply to you.

If the house is tenant-occupied, the buyer will want to know the lease term. Under state law a month-to-month tenancy ends with at least 30 days' notice before the end of a monthly period, and a nonpayment demand allows three days, excluding weekends and court holidays. Give the buyer a copy of the lease early.

Commuters also matter in this market. The Census reports a mean travel time to work of 35.8 minutes for Homestead workers, and buyers often weigh drive time to Miami against price.

sections.h2: How does a deed transfer work and cost in Homestead?
sections.html:
Because Homestead is in Miami-Dade County, the documentary stamp rate differs from the rest of Florida. The Department of Revenue lists 60 cents per $100 for deeds in Miami-Dade, plus a 45 cents per $100 surtax that is not due on a document transferring only a single-family dwelling. Every other county uses 70 cents per $100.

That surtax exemption matters here. If your property is a single-family house, you generally avoid the extra charge, while a duplex or multi-unit building does not fit that description. Ask your closing agent which line applies to your parcel.

All parties to the deed are liable for the tax regardless of who agrees to pay it. The clerk collects it when the deed is recorded. Recording charges under section 28.24 are $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each additional page, plus a $1.00 and $0.50 trust fund charge and a $4 per page technology charge.

Conveyances of land must be in writing with two subscribing witnesses. Plan the signing so two witnesses are present, or use the audio-video option the statute permits.

sections.h2: What does Miami-Dade say about homestead exemptions after a sale?
sections.html:
Owners of the house keep the exemption only while they live there, and the buyer must apply for their own. The Miami-Dade Property Appraiser says applications are due March 1, and late applications can be accepted until the deadline on the TRIM notice, which is generally 25 days after it is mailed.

Florida voters approved Amendment 3 on November 3, 2026, according to the appraiser's homestead page. The page states the maximum non-school exemption is $150,000 for tax year 2027 and $250,000 for tax year 2028 for owners who established Florida residency by December 31, 2026, with different rules for later arrivals. The school-board exemption stays at $25,000. Ask the appraiser how this applies to your buyer rather than assuming it.

State law also resets assessed value on a sale. A change of ownership brings the property to just value on the next January 1, so the buyer's first bill can exceed yours. Save Our Homes limits yearly increases to the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change after that.

sections.h2: What if the Homestead house has liens, a foreclosure or an estate?
sections.html:
• Foreclosure: after final judgment the clerk must set a public sale not less than 20 days and not more than 35 days out unless the plaintiff consents to longer. The high bidder posts a 5 percent deposit, and objections are due within 10 days of the certificate of sale.
  • Probate: the summary route applies when the non-exempt estate is $150,000 or less, or when death occurred more than two years ago. Creditors have the later of three months after first publication of notice or 30 days after service.
  • Unpaid property taxes: delinquent on April 1, with certificates sold by June 1. After two years from April 1 of the issue year, a certificate holder can apply for a tax deed, so address back taxes early.

Florida has no estate tax for deaths after 2004, and personal representatives have not needed to file Form DR-312 or DR-313 since July 1, 2023.

faqs.q: Is the deed tax different in Homestead than in other Florida cities?
faqs.a: Yes, because Homestead is in Miami-Dade County. The Department of Revenue lists 60 cents per $100 plus a 45 cents surtax that is not due when only a single-family dwelling transfers. Most other counties charge 70 cents per $100.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Homestead house if tenants live in it?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer takes the property subject to the lease terms, so provide a copy. Tenancies without a fixed term end on notice set by statute, such as 30 days for month-to-month.

faqs.q: Does the buyer keep my homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. The buyer must file their own application by March 1 for the next tax year, and the assessed value resets to just value after a change of ownership.

faqs.q: What happens to unpaid property taxes on a sale?
faqs.a: The closing agent pays them from your proceeds, so ask the Miami-Dade tax collector for a payoff figure. Taxes are delinquent on April 1, and unpaid items can be sold as tax certificates by June 1.

faqs.q: How long does recording take after signing?
faqs.a: The clerk records the deed and collects the deed tax at that time, so timing depends on the clerk's queue and whether your closing agent files electronically. Ask your closing agent for their typical turnaround.
